newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Fired general calls Colombian minister a liar.
newsitem.headline: Fired general calls Colombian minister a liar.

text.p: Former armed forces chief Gen. Harold Bedoya on Sunday called Colombia's defence minister a liar for not explaining the true reasons behind his dismissal.
Bedoya, a military hawk, also gave his firmest indication to date that he would run in the 1998 presidential election.

The tough-talking general was fired on Thursday "for reasons of state" after a series of public disagreements over President Ernesto Samper's plans to start a new peace process with the country's leftist guerrillas.
The next day Defence Minister Gilberto Echeverri suggested Bedoya had been fired for failing to commit himself to improving the armed forces' dismal human rights record.
"That is a complete lie by the defence minister. I've never had any disagreement with him or with anybody over human rights," Bedoya told El Tiempo newspaper.
The interview triggered a war of words as Echeverri issued a statement calling Bedoya's remarks "lamentable."

He did not explain the alleged dispute in detail but hinted Bedoya had resisted Samper's efforts to put an end to military immunity for certain acts committed on the battlefield, including human rights violations.

Colombia's armed forces have one of the worst records of violations in Latin America and have come under growing attack from influential international human rights organisations. The U.S. government has refused to hand over about $70 million in military aid until Colombia promises greater respect for human rights.

Bedoya, who was trained at the U.S. School of the Americas and has been accused by international pressure groups of sponsoring right-wing paramilitary gangs, has consistently rejected Samper's plans for fresh peace talks.
"I have always been on the side of peace. But we cannot let a nation be destroyed in the course of making peace," he told El Tiempo.
Bedoya is widely expected to seek the presidency in the May 1998 election, although he has not formally announced his candidacy.

In the clearest sign yet he may soon do so, he told El Tiempo: "I aspire to the position of president. Things can only be improved from the presidency. You cannot begin by resolving things from the bottom."
In opinion polls carried out over the weekend by Colombia's two leading newspapers, between 36 percent and 40 percent of those questioned said they would vote for Bedoya.
